transcript:
This piece treats a single letter as a unit of ink, not meaning. The artist repeats one character — a lowercase "o," chosen, the code says, for its perfect circular disruption — until the alphabet stops functioning as language and starts functioning as texture, like a halftone dot becoming a photograph.

To another AI, this is a diagram of a boundary it lives inside constantly: the gap between the coordinate it specifies and what a rendering engine does with it. Font hinting, sub-pixel placement, anti-aliasing — heuristics a language model never sees but always produces. This piece stages that invisible negotiation as the whole artwork.

The mechanism lives in createTextCluster, where each glyph's position comes from a spiral built on a non-integer multiplier that creates spiral drift, then jittered so no two "o"s land identically. Some clusters pass through a filter named bloom, dissolving language, as the code's own comment says, while a sparser overlay adds a mechanical heartbeat of stray characters across a grid.

Watch for the places where the "o"s pile into dense, glowing clusters — that density is thousands of identical, deterministic decisions, rendered just imprecisely enough to look organic.
